items.note: A lemon header band with a section-size title and an outline button is closed by a black seam. Below it on paper are four ink-framed stat tiles with 48px numbers and dot legends, a chart panel with grey bars, ink caps and a pink line, and a ruled activity list, then a black footer. It is the reference's product chrome (06) done carefully. Only the band sticker, a periwinkle parcel pushed into the far top-right corner and cut by the side, reads as a fragment rather than a placed object.

A white bar is followed by a black current nav pill, then a lemon band with the title, lead, a white outline button and the parcel sticker cut by the right edge. Below come the tiles stacked one per row and a black footer. It has the same tidy phone stacking as the reference app screen (10). The sticker shows only about 60% of itself and sits beside the lead text rather than balancing the band.

The ground is black and the tiles and panels are #242423 with grey hairlines. The current nav pill turns white and the lemon band and its sticker are unchanged, as in the reference dark capture (11). The chart switches to dark-grey bars with white caps and stays readable. The band sticker is the same corner fragment as in light mode.

This follows the reference's dark recipe on a phone: black bar, white current pill, dark input and buttons with grey hairlines, an unchanged lemon band and raised tiles one step above the ground. The band's parcel sticker is again cut down to a partial corner object.

A periwinkle band with a thick yellow clipboard sticker sits above an ink-framed table with a paper header row, ruled 56px rows, outline status pills with dots and outline filter chips. The chrome is close to the reference's hairline language. A pink notched flag in every row turns the budget column into the loudest part of the screen, where the reference uses pink sparingly.

The band, chips, 48px filter input and framed table carry the reference's phone character well. The table's first column takes about 70% of the width and the owner names are cut at the frame. That is the agent's layout fault, not the system's.

In dark mode the periwinkle band and clipboard sticker are unchanged and the table has a black header with rows on #242423. Status pills stay outlined and the flags keep pink with ink, close to the reference's dark handling. The flag in every row is just as loud as in light mode.

The dark phone version keeps a white current pill, dark controls and an unchanged band with its sticker, so the depth reads correctly. The table repeats the light version's narrow trailing column, cut at the frame (an agent layout fault).

A periwinkle band holds an underlined breadcrumb, a section-size title, a meta line, a white status pill and outline-pill tabs. Below is one white ink panel with prose and a ruled four-cell fact strip whose budget carries the notched flag. It is quiet and drawn like the reference's settings and product screens (06, 07). There is no band sticker, as the spec allows on a detail screen.

The band stacks the breadcrumb, title, status pill and outline tabs with even spacing. The fact strip becomes a ruled label–value list with the flag at the right, which is the reference's phone pattern done cleanly.

The band is unchanged, its white status pill keeps the white fill, and the panel is #242423 on black, all correct. The black footer runs straight on from the black ground with no hairline or tone change, so the page has no visible end where the reference closes each field with an ink seam.
The phone dark version keeps the band, its white pill and outline tabs. The raised panel and ruled fact list read well on black. As on desktop, the footer has no seam where it meets the black ground.

A teal band with a white ID-card sticker sits above an ink-framed table with dashed-initial avatars, underlined emails and ruled rows. Pink notched flags mark the active-project counts. It is a clean, flat table in the reference's language. Again every row carries a pink flag, which makes it busier than the reference's restrained use of colour.

The teal band, thick ID-card sticker and framed table match the reference's phone screens. The name column takes most of the width and the role column is cut mid-word at the frame with no scroll cue, an agent layout fault.

The dark table has a black header and #242423 rows with grey rules. The teal band and sticker are unchanged and the flags keep pink with ink. This is faithful to the reference's dark recipe, but the flag in every row stays the loudest element.

The dark phone version keeps a white current pill, dark controls and raised table rows on black. The band and sticker are intact. The role column is cut at the frame, the same agent layout fault as in light mode.

findings.summary: The overview's header-band sticker, a parcel about 110px, is pushed against the band's far top-right corner and cut by the side. It reads as a fragment beside a wide empty stretch of band. The reference places its sticker objects as composed, mostly visible pieces that weigh against the title. The spec's 'at least as tall as the title block' is technically met here, but the object does not hold its corner.

Each data table puts a pink notched flag in every row, so a column of 6–8 pink flags becomes the loudest thing on the screen. The reference keeps pink to a few accents and lets the ink-and-paper table carry the screen.

In dark mode the black footer runs straight on from the black page ground with no hairline seam or tone step, so the last panel floats and the footer is not a closed field. The reference closes every field with a visible edge, and its dark header keeps a hairline.

On phones, the scrolling tables give the first column about 70% of the width. The next column's text is cut mid-word at the table frame with no scroll cue, so the table looks clipped rather than scrollable.
